tools.name: kimo_get_state
tools.title: Get Kimo state
tools.description: Start here. Lists every open Kimo document (docId, path, dirty, revision), the selection, top-level nodes with visibility hints, components, a variables/themes summary and other connected agents. Pass docId to describe one document only. Your permissions are in data.you. Then call kimo_read_docs for the schema and ops guides, kimo_open to open a .kimo file, or kimo_query to read nodes.

tools.name: kimo_query
tools.title: Query nodes
tools.description: Declarative read of nodes. select by ids, and/or filter by name (substring, case-insensitive), type, text content, component (instances of), or under (subtree of). depth controls how many levels of children are returned (0 = matched nodes only; elided children show as "…"). resolveVariables replaces $variable refs with values for the given theme; resolveInstances expands instance content as virtual nodes (instanceId/childId). include adds bounds, layout problems (clipping, collapse, missing fonts), path geometry, override origin. Results are a flat list, paginated with cursor. The whole document is never dumped: give at least one selector or under.

tools.name: kimo_apply_ops
tools.title: Edit with typed ops
tools.description: The way to change a document. Sends an ordered list of typed ops applied atomically: all succeed or nothing changes. Ops: insert, update, replace, move, delete, copy, instantiate, make_component, detach, set_override, reset_override, set_args, swap_instance, declare_prop, remove_prop, set_slot, set_variables, set_theme_axes, create_variable, update_variable, rename_variable, delete_variable, set_theme_pin, theme_axis. Give new nodes a key and reference them later in the same call as @key (e.g. insert a frame with key hero, then insert a text node with parent @hero; a text node's string goes in content, not text). Pass baseRevision from your last read to avoid overwriting edits made since (REVISION_CONFLICT). dryRun=true validates and returns the diff without committing; render=true attaches a PNG of the changed top-level frames after commit. Deletes and other destructive ops may ask the user first. Read kimo_read_docs path=ops for examples.

tools.name: kimo_render
tools.title: Render nodes to PNG or SVG
tools.description: Renders nodes to PNG images attached to the result (MCP image content), using the same CanvasKit engine as the canvas. Always reflects every committed edit, including one made earlier in the same turn. Use after building a section to check layout, clipping and contrast. Keep scale modest (images cost tokens): maxSize caps the longest side. format svg returns standalone SVG markup per node in data.images[].svg (the code exporter's SVG, text laid out with the canvas fonts) instead of image content.

tools.name: kimo_history
tools.title: History and undo
tools.description: list: recent op groups with author. undo / redo: undo or redo YOUR OWN last op group (your origin's undo stack; never the user's or another agent's edits). tools.name: kimo_export
tools.title: Export files
tools.description: Deterministic export (export grant needed). png (one file per node, <nodeId>.png) and kimo (the subtrees as a standalone .kimo with the variables they use) are written to outDir (absolute; allow-list applies). Code and token targets — react-tailwind (<Root>.tsx pages, <Component>.tsx per component, tokens.css), html-css (index.html, styles.css, tokens.css), tokens-dtcg (tokens.json), tokens-css, tailwind-theme (@theme), svg (one per root), pdf (one page per root) — are written to outDir when given, otherwise returned inline (contents; pdf as base64). Exact values, variables kept as CSS custom properties unless variables=false. Never overwrites a different file unless overwrite=true (identical files are reported unchanged); nothing is written when any file conflicts. Returns paths with hashes and export issues (approximations).
